definition: Polymorphism in computer science refers to the ability of a function or an object to take on many forms.
details: Polymorphism in computer science refers to the ability of a function or an object to take on many forms. It allows methods to do different things based on the object it is acting upon, essential for achieving abstraction and flexibility in object-oriented programming.

explainer.lead: Polymorphism is the ability of a function or object to take on many forms, letting methods behave differently depending on the object they act upon. It is essential for abstraction and flexibility in object-oriented programming.

tiers.eli5: It's like the word 'draw' meaning different things to a pencil and a card player—same instruction, different result depending on who does it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers rely on it to write code against a common interface while concrete types differ underneath. A pitfall is overusing it, which obscures which implementation actually runs.
tiers.paperLevel: A single interface or name is bound to multiple implementations, resolved by the object's type, giving abstraction and flexibility in object-oriented programming. The mechanism does not by itself guarantee type safety at every call site.

explainer.example: A 'render' method is called on a circle and a square object, and each draws itself differently.
